title: Feed A Crowd: Spanakopita-Style Pasta Bake
subtitle: Cook Once, Serve More!
description: Serve up more with our Feed A Crowd recipes! Using more hearty ingredients like filling carbs, proteins and veggies, you can satisfy extra hungry tummies or keep something for tomorrow’s lunch. If you’re on a 2-person plan, these recipes make 4 portions; on a 4-person plan, they make 8 portions.

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Preheat the oven to 220C, fan-forced (see Feed A Crowd). Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil for the pasta. Grease a 1.5L (6 cup) baking dish. Finely chop the onion. Cut the tomatoes into thin wedges. Coarsely chop three-quarters of the spinach. Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves.
Cook pasta: Cook the pasta in the pan of boiling water for 10 mins or until al dente. Reserve 60ml (¼ cup) cooking water, then drain the pasta.

Make sauce: Meanwhile, heat 1 tbs olive oil in a large deep frypan over medium heat. Cook the onion, stirring, for 3-4 mins until softened. Add the garlic and cumin and coriander spice blend and cook, stirring, for 30 secs or until fragrant. Stir in the cream and 125ml (½ cup) water and bring to a simmer. Cook for 2-3 mins until slightly reduced.

Bake pasta bake: Add the chopped spinach to the sauce and cook, stirring, for 1-2 mins until slightly wilted. Add the pasta and reserved cooking water and toss to combine. Remove the pan from the heat. Taste, then season with salt and pepper. Spoon the pasta mixture into the baking dish. Crumble over the feta and bake for 5-7 mins until golden.

Serve up: While the pasta is baking, combine 2 tsp olive oil and 1 tsp white wine vinegar in a large bowl and season with salt and pepper. Add the tomato and remaining spinach and toss to coat. Divide the pasta bake among plates or pop the dish on the table for everyone to help themselves. Serve with the salad and enjoy!
Feed A Crowd: Don't want to turn the oven on? Instead of making a pasta bake, simply toss the cooked pasta with the spinach sauce and scatter over the crumbled feta to serve.
